speaker: alice
text: Right, let's kick off with some environmental wins that'll put a spring in your step. Queensland's had its wettest year in over a decade, and that means some absolutely spectacular things are happening out west. The Channel Country river systems have flooded magnificently, sending water surging toward Lake Eyre for the biggest floods in 15 years.

speaker: charlie
text: And when Lake Eyre fills up, mate, it's like nature throwing the party of the century. Fish are breeding like mad, waterbirds are flying in from across the continent - it's this massive ecosystem celebration that only happens when the conditions are just right. Shows you how resilient our landscape can be when it gets the water it needs.

speaker: alice
text: Plus closer to home, the Great Barrier Reef is getting some major protection with gill net fishing being phased out by mid-2027. That'll give our threatened species like turtles and dugongs a much better chance of thriving. Sometimes the best environmental news is simply giving nature the space to do what it does best.
